item.title: Benchmark vs ComfyUI — RTX 3090
item.description:
Benchmark vs ComfyUI

ComfyUI and Nox run the same generation jobs on the same machine, so the timings are directly comparable. Each pipeline is generated twice: a Cold run in a fresh process (including model and pipeline load) and a Warm run immediately afterwards. Speedup is calculated as ComfyUI time / Nox time; above 1x means Nox was faster. Both engines load the exact same checkpoints: INT8 ConvRot for every pipeline except SDXL, which runs in FP16 on both.

item.title: Benchmarking Nox against ComfyUI
item.description: A speedup is only meaningful if both sides did the same work. It is easy to make an inference engine look fast: run fewer steps, drop to a lower resolution, swap in a smaller or more aggressively quantized checkpoint, or compare a warm process against a cold one. We wanted the Nox benchmarks to be immune to all of that, so this post explains how the comparison is set up and then shows every output from the latest run next to its ComfyUI counterpart.
